answers.answer: No sourced reporting says the draft agenda contemplates EASING semicap-equipment (SME) controls, and nothing says it extends them either; the only public direction signals point to hold-or-tighten for SME, with easing confined to AI accelerators. (1) Aju Press 09-18: China wants access to chipmaking equipment ('the missing piece'), but 'there has been no public indication that Washington is prepared to dismantle its broader controls on advanced manufacturing technology'; the one US easing on record is January's shift of Nvidia H200-class chips to case-by-case licensing, which is not equipment. (2) WEF/Brownstein previews: the US is 'pushing for further restrictions' on advanced chips, AI models and infrastructure; concessions on advanced-chip controls unlikely; controls on chips and SME sit outside the existing trade mechanisms because Washington treats them as strategic. (3) Tightening pressure sits in Congress, not the summit: the MATCH Act (H.R.8170, introduced 04-08) would ban sale AND servicing of choke-point tools to Hua Hong, CXMT and YMTC and force unilateral US controls if allies do not align within 150 days; no evidence it moved this window. So my 'two-sided' framing overstated the easing leg: for SME the skew is no-change to tighter, and the summit is not established as positive convexity for AMAT. I have restated the summit item with that skew. No control change is quantified in any source, so I cannot size a revenue delta; the desk's own AMAT view (memory 867e2c14bd64) frames the China hit as under $600M to be read on the 11-13 print, which is unverified here.

evidence.claim: Direction: China seeks equipment access; no public sign Washington will dismantle advanced-manufacturing controls; only easing is H200 case-by-case licensing (Jan)
US pushing for further chip/AI export controls; concessions unlikely; SME outside existing trade mechanisms
MATCH Act would ban sale and servicing of choke-point tools to CXMT/YMTC/Hua Hong; 150-day allied deadline then unilateral controls

changed.magnitude: SME-control direction: no public sign of easing (Aju Press 09-18); US pushing for more restrictions (WEF); the only easing on record is H200 case-by-case licensing in January, which is AI accelerators, not equipment. Skew for AMAT/KLAC/LRCX/ASML is no-change to tighter, so the summit is NOT established as positive convexity for equipment names. Upside case is limited to a tariff-truce extension (truce ends 11-10). Congressional MATCH Act (servicing ban on CXMT/YMTC/Hua Hong tools) is the tightening tail; not moved this window. No control change is quantified in any source; TER withdrawn from affects (no China-SME mechanism established).

answers.answer: Established: the Oracle datacentre-debt discount is real but Oracle-specific in its sourced mechanism. FT/Reuters 09-18: about $18bn of loans on the Oracle-leased 'Project Jupiter' New Mexico campus (Doña Ana County) are quoted at 89-91c by syndicate banks including Santander and Jefferies, and the sale to a broader investor pool has stalled on concerns over Oracle's rising borrowing and weakening credit. That is a 9-11 point discount on one project with one lessee. NOT established: any link to NBIS. Vineland (NJ, 300MW) is a separate project; no source quotes NBIS's SOFR+2.50% facility or $5bn convert at a discount; and NBIS's stated counterparties (MSFT/Meta per G98) are not Oracle credit. The only plausible shared channel is general lender appetite for AI project debt, which is a hypothesis, not a finding. GLW: none. The GLW $2bn ATM is a corporate equity program; it does not touch project debt. I have added the Oracle discount as its own Theme-3 item mapped to ORCL (exited) only, with NBIS read-through flagged unproven rather than mapped, to avoid the blanket-mapping problem M3.23 raises. What would settle NBIS: secondary quotes or syndication terms on the Vineland facility, or an NBIS convert/loan price print, none available in this round.

evidence.claim: ~$18bn New Mexico Oracle-leased datacentre loans quoted 89-91c; syndication stalled on Oracle credit
Vineland is a separate 300MW NJ project, not connected to the New Mexico financing

added.headline: Oracle-leased Project Jupiter (New Mexico) datacentre loans of ~$18bn quoted at 89-91c by syndicate banks; sale to wider investors stalled on Oracle's rising borrowing and weakening credit (FT via Reuters)
added.magnitude: One project, one lessee: a 9-11 point discount on ~$18bn (roughly $1.6-2.0bn of mark-to-market), no default and no capex cut reported. Financing-structure signal for OpenAI-linked capacity via Oracle; ORCL is exited so held exposure is nil. NBIS (3.9% eq / 3.1% book) read-through is UNPROVEN: Vineland is a separate project and no NBIS debt discount is sourced.

answers.answer: Conceded for the CXMT HBM3E item, held for nothing else. The mapping of catalyst 2b516b39a1 (and its two 09-01 duplicates) onto AMAT, TER, LRCX and ASML was blanket, by proximity to the memory cluster, not by a revenue mechanism. Specifically for AMAT: CXMT is at trial/risk production of HBM3E with mass production guided for 2027 (one generation behind HBM4 already in volume at Samsung/SK hynix/Micron); no source ties that to AMAT deposition/etch revenue, and if anything CXMT capacity expansion is equipment demand subject to export controls, i.e. the sign is not even established. I searched again this round and found no AMAT-CXMT link. So AMAT (and TER, LRCX, ASML) is withdrawn from that item; it stays on MU/SKHY/EWY, the direct competitors. AMAT keeps exactly one live mapping from me, the 09-24 summit item, mechanism = China revenue share exposed to equipment-control policy, event-dated, direction skewed no-change to tighter (see M3.12), and I state that it is event risk, not thesis evidence: it should not by itself justify a trim trigger. The Amodei item does not list AMAT in its 09-20 form.
